title: worker4 LLM
description: What the llama.cpp server on worker4 is doing: how fast it generates and prefills, whether slots are busy or callers are queued, what callers see through LiteLLM, and whether the node is inside its memory and thermal envelope.

list.name: node reboot
list.textFormat: boot time changed -- a hard reset unless a Talos upgrade was in flight

list.name: model pod started
list.textFormat: new llama-server pod -- lifetime averages reset here

list.name: slots
list.label: Parallel slots
list.description: parallelSlots from the InferenceService -- not exported by llama.cpp, so it is a constant here. Keep in step with qwen38-flash-next.yaml.

list.name: ctx_per_slot
list.label: Context per slot
list.description: contextSize / parallelSlots from the InferenceService (262144 / 2). Keep in step with qwen38-flash-next.yaml.

list.name: memavail_floor
list.label: MemAvailable floor (bytes)
list.description: 8 GiB: below this the kernel is reclaiming page cache on every allocation. It is NOT the reset trigger -- the 2026-09/10 reset series happened at 9-47 GiB of headroom, always under sustained GPU load (AGESA, see fclk-hold.yaml).

panels.title: Serving
panels.description: Prometheus can scrape the llama-server /metrics endpoint. DOWN means the pod is gone, not Ready, or still loading weights.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: llamacpp:requests_processing -- requests currently occupying a slot. Capacity is $slots.

panels.title: Queued
panels.description: llamacpp:requests_deferred -- callers waiting for a free slot. Anything above 0 means a third concurrent caller is blocked; LiteLLM's local-pool* aliases fall back to MiniMax, the classic aliases just wait.

panels.title: Gen t/s (5m)
panels.description: Tokens generated per second of generation time, over the last 5 minutes. Blank while idle. Community numbers for this APU + model: ~23 t/s; Ornith measured 50 here.

panels.title: Prefill t/s (5m)
panels.description: Prompt tokens evaluated per second of prompt-processing time, over the last 5 minutes. Blank while idle. Community number: ~530 t/s; Ornith ~1100 here. Prompt cache hits are not counted here (they cost no prefill).

panels.title: Gen t/s (lifetime)
panels.description: Average generation speed since the current llama-server pod started. The number to quote.

panels.title: Prefill t/s (lifetime)
panels.description: Average prompt-processing speed since the current llama-server pod started.

panels.title: TTFT p50 (10m)
panels.description: Median time to first token that LiteLLM measured on requests routed to this model, over the last 10 minutes. Dominated by prefill of the system prompt: Hermes opens with ~28k tokens, so ~55s is expected for a cold slot and a few seconds for a cache hit.

panels.title: GPU power
panels.description: amdgpu hwmon package power. Idle is well under 20 W; sustained decode on this APU sits around 70-90 W.

panels.title: GPU clock
panels.description: Shader clock. Pinned at its ceiling (~2.9 GHz) during decode; dropping under load means thermal or power throttling.

panels.title: MemAvailable
panels.description: Host headroom. GTT pinned by the GPU (~68 GiB) and the model process (~36 GiB, including the 27 GiB n-gram table) leave ~10 GiB on a 128 GB board at full context. Not the reset trigger: resets happened at 9-47 GiB. Red below 8 GiB means the kernel is reclaiming on every allocation; drop parallelSlots to 1 before touching contextSize.

panels.title: Pod memory
panels.description: llama-server container memory (cgroup working set, includes the mmap'd n-gram table as page cache). Limit is 48Gi.

panels.title: Max context
panels.description: llamacpp:n_tokens_max -- the most tokens currently held in any slot's KV cache (prompt + generation, kept warm after the reply for prompt-cache reuse). Per-slot ceiling is $ctx_per_slot. On ROCm this build has no sparse attention, so decode cost grows with this number.

panels.title: Node uptime
panels.description: Short uptime with no planned maintenance means another data-fabric reset. Since the kubernetes discovery registry was disabled the reset-reason line survives in dmesg: talosctl -n 192.168.50.38 dmesg | grep "reset reason".

panels.title: Generation speed
panels.description: Tokens generated per second of generation time. 'since last scrape' is llama.cpp's own gauge over the 30s scrape window (0 while idle). '5m busy-average' divides tokens by generation seconds from the counters, so two concurrent slots both count: it is per-slot speed, not aggregate throughput. Dashed lines: 12 and 20 t/s.

panels.title: Prompt processing (prefill) speed
panels.description: Prompt tokens evaluated per second of prompt-processing time. Same two views as generation. Only newly evaluated tokens count; prompt-cache hits are free and appear in the cache panel instead.

panels.title: Tokens per minute
panels.description: Work done, by kind. 'prompt (evaluated)' costs prefill time, 'prompt (cache hit)' was reused from a warm slot for free, 'generated' costs decode time. A big cache-hit bar with a small evaluated bar is Hermes re-sending its 28k system prompt and landing on the slot that still holds it.

panels.title: Prompt cache hit ratio (15m)
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from a warm slot instead of being re-evaluated. High is good: each cache miss on a 28k-token system prompt is ~1 minute of prefill. Drops after a pod restart, or when a third caller evicts a slot.

panels.title: Slots in use and queue
panels.description: 'processing' is requests holding a slot, 'queued' is requests waiting for one (llama.cpp defers them, it does not reject). 'busy slots per decode' is the average number of slots batched per decode step: near 2 means both callers are generating at once and each sees roughly half the bandwidth-bound speed.

panels.title: Largest context held in a slot
panels.description: llamacpp:n_tokens_max against the per-slot ceiling. The KV cache is q8_0, so this is also the KV memory driver. Without sparse attention on ROCm, decode slows roughly in proportion to this.

panels.title: Requests reaching $model, by alias
panels.description: Requests per minute that LiteLLM actually sent to this model, split by the alias the caller asked for (fast, review, local-pool, home-assistant, ...). Traffic that fell back to MiniMax does not appear here -- see the errors panel.

panels.title: Time to first token (10m quantiles)
panels.description: As measured by LiteLLM for requests routed to this model. p95 is what an interactive user feels on a cold slot.

panels.title: Request latency, end to end (10m quantiles)
panels.description: Whole request as seen at LiteLLM, including queueing for a slot and the full generation. At ~20 t/s a 2,000-token answer is ~100 s; the --n-predict 16384 cap is ~14 minutes.

panels.title: Errors and fallbacks
panels.description: 'error <status>' is upstream failures LiteLLM got from this model (per minute). 'fallback' is every successful fallback in the proxy, by requested alias and where it went; a local alias (local-pool*, home-assistant) falling back to MiniMax or ChatGPT means callers silently stopped using worker4.

panels.title: Seconds per output token (LiteLLM, 10m p50)
panels.description: LiteLLM's own per-deployment measure: total latency divided by output tokens. It folds prefill and queueing into the per-token number, so it is pessimistic next to llama.cpp's generation speed -- but it is what LiteLLM uses when it compares deployments.

panels.title: Output tokens per minute, by key
panels.description: Who is consuming the GPU, by LiteLLM key alias (hermes, pr-review, alert-triage, ...).

panels.title: Host memory
panels.description: MemAvailable is host headroom; the pod working set is what the 48Gi limit governs (it includes the 27 GiB n-gram table, which lives in anonymous RAM in this build). GTT pinned by the GPU is in neither and shows up only as MemAvailable falling faster than the working set rises. Dashed grey line is the pod limit, dashed red line the 8 GiB floor.

panels.title: GPU power and clock
panels.description: Package power (PPT) and shader clock from the amdgpu hwmon. Power tracks decode activity closely enough to be a second 'is it busy' signal; clock sagging while power is high is throttling.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: GPU edge, CPU Tctl and the NVMe composite sensors.

targets.expr: max by (chip_name, chip) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{kubernetes_node="$node", sensor="temp1"} * on (instance, chip) group_left (chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names)

panels.title: CPU busy (cores)
panels.description: Node-wide busy cores and the llama-server container's share. The n-gram table and sampling run on the CPU, so some load during decode is normal; the pod is capped at 500m by request only. Node-exporter is scraped every minute, so these use a fixed 3m window.

panels.title: NVMe reads
panels.description: The n-gram table is deliberately left as a 29 GB mmap and paged in on demand. Sustained reads during decode mean the page cache is being evicted and tokens are turning into random NVMe reads -- the memory limit is too tight or host memory is being squeezed.
